title: Amazon SNS and EventBridge
description: Learn to build event-driven architectures using SNS pub/sub messaging and EventBridge rules, event buses, and schedules.

data.text: Amazon SNS and EventBridge are the building blocks of event-driven architectures on AWS. SNS uses a pub/sub model to push messages to multiple subscribers. EventBridge routes events based on rules, letting you build complex, decoupled workflows.
SNS topics act as access points for publishers and subscribers. A publisher sends a message to a topic, and SNS pushes the message to all subscribed endpoints. This pattern is called fanout.

data.title: SNS Subscription Types
items: **HTTP/HTTPS endpoints** — for webhooks and external integrations

data.text: SNS supports message filtering at the subscription level. You can attach a filter policy to a subscription so it only receives messages that match specific attributes. This lets multiple consumers subscribe to the same topic but receive only the messages they care about.

EventBridge is a serverless event bus. It receives events from AWS services, SaaS partners, and custom applications. Rules match incoming events and route them to targets like Lambda, SNS, SQS, or Step Functions.

data.title: EventBridge Key Concepts
items: **Event buses** — default bus for AWS events; custom buses for your own applications
**Rules** — match incoming events and send to targets
**Event schemas** — validate event structure using OpenAPI schemas
**Scheduled events** — run Lambda or Step Functions on a cron schedule
**Schema Registry** — discover and share event schemas across teams

data.title: SNS vs EventBridge
data.text: Use SNS when you want simple pub/sub with fanout to multiple endpoints. Use EventBridge when you need filtering, schema validation, scheduled events, or SaaS integrations.

terms.definition: A logical access point that aggregates published messages and delivers them to subscribers.
An architectural pattern where a single message is broadcast to multiple recipients.
A filter that matches incoming events and routes them to specified targets.
A pipeline that receives and delivers events. The default bus receives AWS service events; custom buses receive application events.

data.title: Create an Event-Driven Workflow
data.description: Create an EventBridge rule that triggers a Lambda function every hour and another rule that triggers on S3 object creation.
steps: Create an EventBridge rule with a cron schedule
Target a Lambda function that writes to CloudWatch Logs
Create a second rule for S3 object-created events
Target a different Lambda function that reads the S3 object metadata
Test both rules by creating an S3 object and waiting for the schedule
data.expectedOutcome: Both scheduled and event-driven rules trigger their Lambda functions correctly.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SNS pushes messages to subscribers using a pub/sub model
EventBridge routes events based on content rules
Scheduled events let you run code on a cron-like schedule
Both services enable event-driven, decoupled architectures
data.takeaway: SNS and EventBridge remove the need for polling and tight coupling. Your services react to events instead of constantly checking for updates.
